label: Agriculture & fishing
scope: Farming, forestry and fishing; Defra evidence here is farming only.
actors: Defra is the statistics/public-policy actor; current named forestry/fishing enterprises and buyer concentration not acquired.

pestle.Political: Not acquired for this sector: current subsidy scheme and claimant scope.
pestle.Technological: Not acquired for this sector: measured farm automation cost/yield outcomes.
pestle.Legal: Not acquired for this sector: applicable land, labour and environmental duties by jurisdiction.
pestle.Economic: Official section output -2.2% September yoy; 2024 GVA share 0.7%. DEFRA-A25 reports improved aggregate farming GVA but a non-positive FBI minority; scope excludes forestry/fishing.
pestle.Social: Interpretation: a farm-income distribution question is warranted; matched farm-type and household-income evidence is still absent.
pestle.Environmental: DEFRA farm-income evidence does not identify climate causation. Test water/feed/yield exposure at a named farm segment.

relational_swot.strength_context: 2025 farming income rose; 21% loss incidence cannot be extended to every farm or all section A.
relational_swot.weakness: No sector-wide internal weakness established; Acquire matched farm-type cash/output/input series and named processor/supplier contracts; separate GB FBI from UK and fishing/forestry.
relational_swot.external_opportunity_hypothesis: Which farm segment has a demonstrated cash or productivity constraint after subsidies, input costs and diversification?
relational_swot.threat_to_test: Energy/feed/fertiliser costs can alter farm returns; no named contracts. Processor/retailer concentration is a bargaining hypothesis pending segment data.

five_forces.rivalry: Commodity rivalry differs by crop/livestock and season.
five_forces.new_entrants: Land, skills and capital constrain entry; current barriers unmeasured.
five_forces.substitutes: Imports and diet choices are potential substitutes, not measured displacement.
five_forces.supplier_power: Energy/feed/fertiliser costs can alter farm returns; no named contracts.
five_forces.buyer_power: Processor/retailer concentration is a bargaining hypothesis pending segment data.

value_chain: Land, labour, inputs and water → crops/livestock → processors/retail. Commodity output, subsidies and diversification differ from farm profit.
strategic_questions: Which farm segment has a demonstrated cash or productivity constraint after subsidies, input costs and diversification?
decision_role_hypotheses: Farm owner/finance and agricultural-processor operations roles
counter_evidence_and_limits: 2025 farming income rose; 21% loss incidence cannot be extended to every farm or all section A.
next_research: Acquire matched farm-type cash/output/input series and named processor/supplier contracts; separate GB FBI from UK and fishing/forestry.

label: Energy supply
scope: Electricity/gas generation, networks and supply; GB default-tariff retail evidence excludes NI and non-domestic pricing.
actors: Ofgem is the GB regulator. Current named generator/network/supplier comparisons are not acquired in this tranche.

pestle.Technological: Not acquired for this sector: named generation/network/supply asset performance.

pestle.Political: The regulated cap transmits wholesale/network costs through a specific retail mechanism; it is not a sector profit guarantee.
pestle.Legal: Cap applicability is GB default domestic tariffs; NI, fixed and non-domestic contracts are distinct.
pestle.Social: Interpretation: affordability should be tested against usage, support and household income, not a notional typical bill.

relational_swot.strength_context: A cap increase is not each household bill increase or proof of supplier loss; fixed tariffs and hedges can limit effects.
relational_swot.weakness: No sector-wide internal weakness established; Acquire named supplier/customer outcomes, hedge coverage and approved network-investment delivery choices; distinguish electricity policy from energy-price shock.
relational_swot.external_opportunity_hypothesis: Which customer or asset decision is exposed after actual hedging, tariff and network arrangements?
relational_swot.threat_to_test: Wholesale fuel, network and meter dependencies matter; exposure needs contracts/hedges. Household switching differs from industrial contracting power.

five_forces.rivalry: Retail rivalry differs from regulated network monopolies.
five_forces.new_entrants: Licences, network assets and funding shape entry.
five_forces.substitutes: Efficiency/self-generation alter purchased energy; effect depends on load/tariff.
five_forces.supplier_power: Wholesale fuel, network and meter dependencies matter; exposure needs contracts/hedges.
five_forces.buyer_power: Household switching differs from industrial contracting power.

value_chain: Generate/transport/retail energy → metered use and settlement; regulated allowances, hedging and customer charges are different value mechanisms.
strategic_questions: Which customer or asset decision is exposed after actual hedging, tariff and network arrangements?
decision_role_hypotheses: Energy treasury, network asset, retail product and customer operations roles
counter_evidence_and_limits: A cap increase is not each household bill increase or proof of supplier loss; fixed tariffs and hedges can limit effects.
next_research: Acquire named supplier/customer outcomes, hedge coverage and approved network-investment delivery choices; distinguish electricity policy from energy-price shock.
